title: Web Components Small Examples
description: Use these small Web Components examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Make your own HTML tag
examples.description: A custom element is an HTML tag you define.
examples.code:
<hello-reader></hello-reader>
<script>
  class HelloReader extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() { this.textContent = "Hello, reader!"; }
  }
  customElements.define("hello-reader", HelloReader);
</script>
examples.output: The custom tag shows Hello, reader! after it is connected to the page.

examples.title: Know when an element connects
examples.description: connectedCallback runs when a custom element joins a document.
examples.code:
<visit-note></visit-note>
<script>
  class VisitNote extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() { this.textContent = "I am on the page."; }
  }
  customElements.define("visit-note", VisitNote);
</script>
examples.output: The note writes its message once it is on the page.

examples.title: Read an attribute
examples.description: An attribute is an extra fact written in a tag.
examples.code:
<reader-name name="Mia"></reader-name>
<script>
  class ReaderName extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() { this.textContent = "Hi, " + (this.getAttribute("name") || "reader"); }
  }
  customElements.define("reader-name", ReaderName);
</script>
examples.output: The tag shows Hi, Mia. Without the name attribute, it uses reader.

examples.title: Watch an attribute change
examples.description: observedAttributes names the attributes a custom element watches.
examples.code:
<score-note score="2"></score-note>
<script>
  class ScoreNote extends HTMLElement {
    static observedAttributes = ["score"];
    attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) { this.textContent = "Score: " + newValue; }
  }
  customElements.define("score-note", ScoreNote);
  document.querySelector("score-note").setAttribute("score", "5");
</script>
examples.output: The component ends with Score: 5. Its watched score attribute causes the update.

examples.title: Create a shadow tree
examples.description: A shadow root is a separate group of page parts inside an element.
examples.code:
<shadow-note></shadow-note>
<script>
  class ShadowNote extends HTMLElement {
    constructor() {
      super();
      const root = this.attachShadow({ mode: "open" });
      const paragraph = document.createElement("p");
      paragraph.textContent = "Inside the component";
      root.append(paragraph);
    }
  }
  customElements.define("shadow-note", ShadowNote);
</script>
examples.output: The note displays a paragraph kept inside its shadow root.

examples.title: Keep component styles together
examples.description: Styles inside a shadow root usually apply to its internal elements.
examples.code: Outside note
examples.output: Only Inside note gets this green rule. The outside paragraph keeps its own style.

examples.title: Leave a slot for content
examples.description: A slot is a place where the user of a component can supply content.
examples.code: A story about the moon
examples.output: The card heading is followed by A story about the moon, the content supplied between its tags.

examples.title: Give slots names
examples.description: Named slots let a component accept different pieces of content in different places.
examples.code:
Moon Trip

A space story.
examples.output: Moon Trip fills the named title slot. The paragraph fills the default slot.

examples.title: Share a JavaScript property
examples.description: A property can accept a JavaScript value on an element.
examples.code:
<point-display></point-display>
<script>
  class PointDisplay extends HTMLElement {
    set points(value) { this.textContent = "Points: " + Number(value); }
  }
  customElements.define("point-display", PointDisplay);
  document.querySelector("point-display").points = 7;
</script>
examples.output: The component shows Points: 7 after the property assignment.

examples.title: Send a custom event
examples.description: A custom event lets a component tell its surroundings that something happened.
examples.output: Clicking the internal button sends book-chosen. The outer listener shows Moon Trip.

examples.title: Clean up a repeating job
examples.description: disconnectedCallback runs when a custom element leaves the document.
examples.code:
<tick-note></tick-note>
<script>
  class TickNote extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() { this.count = 0; this.timer = setInterval(() => { this.textContent = String(++this.count); }, 1000); }
    disconnectedCallback() { clearInterval(this.timer); }
  }
  customElements.define("tick-note", TickNote);
</script>
examples.output: The number grows once per second. Removing the element stops its timer.

examples.title: Style the host with a theme value
examples.description: The :host selector styles the custom element itself.
examples.code:
<style>themed-note { --note-colour: navy; }</style><themed-note></themed-note>
<script>
  class ThemedNote extends HTMLElement {
    constructor() { super(); this.attachShadow({mode:"open"}).innerHTML = "<style>:host { display:block; color:var(--note-colour, green); padding:1rem; }</style>Read a story today."; }
  }
  customElements.define("themed-note", ThemedNote);
</script>
examples.output: The custom element has padding and navy text. If the custom property is missing, it uses green.
